title: Codex to Opus Agent Delegation
desc: Agent.cmd lets Codex spawn Opus/Sonnet/Haiku subagents through the same brief-guard and spec-gate as Claude Code Agent() calls. Codex becomes orchestrator, Opus handles judgment.
steps: CHAIN: Codex (cheap execution) -> Agent.cmd stdin JSON -> wkharness brief-guard + spec-gate -> wkclaude.cmd --model opus prompt -> Opus result back to Codex -> Codex implements.
INTERFACE: {tool_name:'Agent', tool_input:{prompt:'SPEC block + 3 skill refs + task', model:'opus'}}. model aliases: opus/sonnet/haiku -> full claude model ID.
GUARDS FIRED: brief-guard requires 3 wkappbot skill read refs in prompt. spec-gate requires SPEC 1-5 numbered block for Opus. Both enforced identically to Claude Code Agent() calls.
Agent.cmd'. JSON prompt must contain SPEC block (for Opus) then skill refs then task. Same rules as Claude Code Agent() -- no shortcuts.
MODEL ROUTING: opus -> claude-opus-4-7. sonnet -> claude-sonnet-4-6. haiku -> claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 (default). Full model IDs passed through unchanged.
EXECUTION: Agent.ps1 extracts prompt+model, calls wkclaude.cmd -Model modelId prompt. wkclaude runs claude --print non-interactive. Output streams to Codex stdout.

DIVISION OF LABOR: Codex=cheap executor (file edits, shell, search). Agent.cmd+Opus=judgment (architecture, root-cause, design). Codex calls Opus only when genuinely stuck or need planning -- same escalation rule as Claude Code.
author: claude
